blogTitle: What Wall Art Should Guys Choose for Apartments?
videoTitle: What Wall Art Should Guys Choose for Apartments?
script:
What Wall Art Should Guys Choose for Apartments?

You know that feeling when you move into a new flat and the walls just… stare back at you? [warmly] Yeah — most guys I work with tell me wall art feels like a minefield. So let's fix that.

The styles that work BEST in a guy's apartment are the ones that feel intentional — black-and-white photography, architectural line art, abstract geometric prints, typographic posters, vintage maps… clean, strong, and actually meaningful to you.

Here's the thing — a pro tip I always give: stick to a maximum of TWO or three styles across your whole flat, otherwise the walls end up looking like a car boot sale.

Before you buy ANYTHING, look at what's already in the room — your sofa colour, your flooring, your furniture style — and let that lead you, not fight against you.

Ask yourself: what's the dominant colour in this room? Is the wall big enough for what I'm buying? And honestly — am I getting this because I LOVE it, or just because it fills a gap?

[warmly] Now, room by room — your living room is the place for a STATEMENT piece: bold photography or a strong architectural print above the sofa does the job every time.

The bedroom? Keep it calmer — softer tones, maybe a landscape or an abstract piece above the headboard; and the home office is perfect for typographic prints or sports photography, properly framed.

When it comes to themes and aesthetics — industrial, minimalist, retro, sports — just pick the one that ALREADY matches your furniture and double down on it.

Here's a little tip I love: hang your art so the centre of the piece sits at eye level — roughly 145 to 150 centimetres from the floor — and always measure BEFORE you put a nail in the wall.

Budget doesn't have to mean boring — digital prints, independent sellers, and limited-edition photography sites can all give you something genuinely ORIGINAL for a fraction of gallery prices.

Scale is everything, right? A small print on a big wall just looks… lost. As a rough rule — a sofa wall needs art that fills at LEAST two-thirds of the sofa's width.

Gallery walls are brilliant — but only if you plan the layout on the FLOOR first, then transfer it to the wall. That's how you avoid a wall full of random holes.

Industrial flat? Go dark metal frames and urban photography. Minimalist? One clean oversized print, loads of negative space. Retro? Warm wood frames and vintage travel prints. Sports-themed office? Frame it PROPERLY — that's what makes it look considered rather than just tacked up.

Skip the big-box retailers and look at independent print studios and specialty art sites — that's where you find pieces that actually START a conversation rather than blend into the background.

[excited] Okay — a set of three London photography prints like this one? Instantly pulls a living room together, works with almost any colour palette, and gives you that clean editorial look without any effort.

Abstract clock prints bring in personality and a bit of graphic boldness — this set of THREE looks brilliant in a modern living room or home office when the frames line up perfectly.

Sacred geometry prints — these feel genuinely considered, right? They add colour and depth without being too literal, and that makes them surprisingly versatile across different room styles.

Urban skyscraper prints are one of my FAVOURITES for an industrial-style flat — that mix of bold architectural lines and city energy is exactly the kind of intentional look that works straight out of the box.

[warmly] This contemporary skyscraper set works beautifully if your flat leans more modern than industrial — softer tones, cleaner lines, and still that strong city subject matter that actually means something.

And for a hallway? A set of TWO urban skyscraper prints is honestly perfect — they fill a narrow wall without overwhelming the space and give every person who walks in an instant first impression.

So there you have it — start with ONE statement piece, match it to what's already in the room, and build from there. Blank walls are honestly just waiting to become the best part of your flat.

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
